subject: Residency ops simulation: EU/APAC failover validation
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Suzanne Klein <suzanne.klein@eurobank.com>, Infra Eng Team <infra-eng@eurobank.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 09:08:00 -0800
Subject: Residency ops simulation: EU/APAC failover validation

Hi Suzanne and team,

Per our call last week, we'd like to run a staged ops simulation to validate our EU->APAC failover and failback behavior for your private deployment (VPC). Goal: confirm data residency guarantees are preserved during a controlled partial outage, and validate proof-of-residency artifacts you require for audit.

High-level ask: can EuroBank join a dry-run window the week of Dec 7 (two-hour slot)? We propose the following scope:
- Run canary failover for a subset of tenants (no more than 10%)
- Validate KV/TTL preservation and prefix cache behavior
- Measure cross-region latency and verify no persistent writes leave primary region
- Collect the following artifacts: request traces, S3 object access logs, control-plane audit events, and signed proof-of-residency report

Attached: residency-sim-plan.xlsx (walkthrough + rollback steps).

Please confirm who from your infra and legal teams should be on the call and any additional acceptance criteria.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Senior Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference

From: Suzanne Klein <suzanne.klein@eurobank.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: Infra Eng Team <infra-eng@eurobank.com>, legal@acme-corp.com
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 17:12:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Residency ops simulation: EU/APAC failover validation

Jonas — thanks, this looks sensible. We can do a two-hour dry-run on Dec 8 at 09:00 CET. Attendees from our side: myself, head of infra (infra-eng@eurobank.com) and compliance (compliance.audit@eurobank.com). Legal (legal@acme-corp.com) is CC'd for the residency evidence format — we need the report to include hash-signed timestamps and a registry of control-plane operations.

A few non-negotiables from EuroBank:
- No customer data may be written to the target (APAC) persistent store — only proxy/cache reads allowed during the simulation
- We require a signed proof-of-residency PDF and the audit log bundle within 24h of the window
- Network peering changes must be reversible without touching routing beyond our isolated test ASNs

We'll review the attachment and follow up if anything in the plan breaks these constraints.

—Suzanne
Director, Platform Operations
EuroBank

Date: Wed, 2 Dec 2026 08:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Residency ops simulation: EU/APAC failover validation

Thanks Jonas — I reviewed the plan and added a couple of technical clarifications in the attached net-diagram-v2.png and inline comments in the spreadsheet:
- We will run prefix caching only for read-paths in APAC; write-paths will be blackholed (return 503) to ensure no persistence outside EU for the dry-run
- KV cache warm-up: schedule preload for the selected tenant set 2 hours before the window to avoid cold-start behavior skewing metrics
- BGP/NAT changes: we'll request ephemeral peering on your side; EuroBank must confirm the ASNs and exact prefixes we may advertise for the test
- Failback plan: explicit step to clear transient logs and rotate signing keys used for the proof-of-residency bundle to prevent stale signatures

Attachment: net-diagram-v2.png (network sequence and where control-plane hooks will trigger).

Laura Bennett
Principal Cloud Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>

Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 3 Dec 2026 06:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Residency ops simulation: EU/APAC failover validation

Couple operational items from my side:
- Runbook checklist: rollout canary -> run synthetic traffic -> collect traces -> validate audit bundle -> failback -> postmortem. I'll draft an RFC runbook and link it to INF-3421.
- Procurement note: ephemeral cross-region peering and additional egress will incur charges; legal/procurement must sign the residency amendment (attached docusign-residency-amendment.pdf) before we change peering.
- Monitoring: enable token-level tracing and per-route byte counters for the window; retention of those traces for 7 days minimum so EuroBank compliance can extract artifacts.

I will also add a pre-run tabletop at T-48h to walk through abort criteria. Marcus — can you confirm SRE on-call availability and whether we can reserve the slot?

Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Production Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: marcus_lin@redwood.com <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, jonas.weber@redwood.com
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 3 Dec 2026 15:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Residency ops simulation: EU/APAC failover validation

Acknowledged — SRE can cover the Dec 8 09:00 CET window. A couple quick points:
- Acceptance criteria for the dry-run (PASS): proof-of-residency bundle contains signed timestamps for all control-plane actions, no customer writes persisted in APAC, and latency increase for affected requests under 250ms p95.
- Abort criteria: any unplanned persistent write to APAC OR failure to produce the audit bundle within 24h -> immediate abort and rollback.
- Postmortem: deliverable within 48 hours, include token-level cost delta and a remediation plan for any edge-case that allowed writes to leak.

I'll add the RFC runbook to INF-3421 and invite SRE on-call for the T-48h tabletop.

Marcus Lin
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference
